# Embassy 4.2.0 — every broker in one window

4.2 turns `embassy tui` into a single pane of glass over every machine in your `nodes.json`.

**What you see** — a host overview at the top, one line per broker with its own health and the age of its last observation, and a detail pane for the selected host with that broker's endpoints, deliveries, and retirements. `[` and `]` switch hosts. The local broker keeps its one-second polling; each remote broker is read over the same plain SSH your federation already uses, every few seconds, independently. A hung or unreachable machine goes visibly stale with the exact code and a next step, and never blocks the local pane or your keyboard.

**What you can do** — the same operator verbs on the selected host: refresh, loopback check, delivery lookup, and retirement. Retiring a remote endpoint confirms on a screen that names the host and the full endpoint ID, then runs that machine's own CLI over SSH; a pane switch or a later poll cannot change the target, and an action whose reply is lost is reported as uncertain rather than replayed.

**What stays true** — metadata only, no bodies, no raw SSH output on screen; "not a provider readiness proof" on every pane; a remote broker's version is shown only as CLI metadata when its reply is not understood, never guessed. Without an interactive terminal, `tui` prints the local status text once and spawns no SSH. No broker state, protocol, dependency, or background process was added.

**Also in 4.2** — the Claude socket post-connect timeout test no longer depends on a scheduling window; one flake seen on the 4.1.0 release run, classified as a test race with no runtime change.

**Upgrading from 4.1.0** — install and restart the broker on each machine; no state reset. From 3.x, follow the reset-only procedure in the 4.0.0 notes.

**Tested with** (m5dev and a laptop over SSH, 2026-09-06): both panes live from one terminal, a stranded Codex endpoint on the laptop retired from m5dev through the host-and-ID confirmation and confirmed retired in the laptop's own ledger, and the same screen with the laptop off the network showing a stale pane while the local pane kept polling. Offline suite 353/353.
